title: ChitUI: a browser dashboard for resin printers

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You have a resin 3D printer on your network, and you'd love to run it from a browser tab. ChitUI does exactly that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So no vendor app, just a web page?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. It's a web control interface for Chitubox resin printers that speak the SDCP three point zero protocol. A small Python process serves the web pages and finds printers on the local network by itself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And when I click a button in the browser?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Python side translates that action into the printer's own language and sends it over the network. The browser never talks to the machine directly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Handy. Anything to make it easy to run?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a Docker option, and it's a fork with the upstream work credited. Most of the code is JavaScript for the interface, with Python as the bridge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full write-up covers the components if you want the layout.
